doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Encouraging students
summary: Teaching as privilege, caring about character, and hoping students recognize Strayhorn and Stolen Moments.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yeah, you just have to eat it in front of them and, “Boy, I wish you could share in this.”

Oh yeah. But encouraging young people to me is a privilege. Because a lot of these kids have no clue, like I said before. And I told them, I said my class is important but I’m more interested in your character and your integrity and your development as a person. If you do that that’s all I care about. In my jazz for listening class I said my goal for you is this: if you’re at a restaurant with your parents, and you hear “Take the A Train” and somebody says, “Why that’s Duke Ellington’s ‘Take the A Train.’” You say, “No that’s Billy Strayhorn’s ‘Take the A Train’” If you’ve got knowledge like that, or if you’re in © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

an airport and you hear, “Oh boy that sounds like Professor Nelson’s Dad’s ‘Stolen Moments.” That’s what I’m looking for for those kids, to introduce them to the music and to keep that little flame going.
I’ll drink to that. But not too much.
That’s right. Not too much. You’ve got to be careful with it.
